summary: The Shanghai Government Scholarship is run by the Shanghai Municipal Education Commission for international students who study at one of 31 listed higher education institutions in Shanghai. It is open to non-Chinese citizens in good health at pre-college, undergraduate, master's and doctoral level. There are two award types: Type A, which covers tuition, accommodation, a monthly living allowance and medical insurance, and Type B, which covers tuition and medical insurance. Each university runs its own application window and selection.
eligibility_notes:
Applicants must be non-Chinese citizens in good health (one university states good physical and mental health) who apply to a participating Shanghai institution.

Education and age: undergraduate applicants need a high school diploma or above and should generally be 25 or under (one university writes under 25). Master's applicants need a bachelor's degree or above and should be 35 or under. Doctoral applicants need a master's degree or above, must show academic research ability and should be 40 or under. Pre-college applicants need a high school diploma, must be under 23 and must already hold a pre-admission letter for an undergraduate programme at a Shanghai university. The Commission pages say the age limits apply as a general guide.

Academics and language: outstanding academic performance and strong study potential are expected. Applicants should generally have HSK level 4 (a certificate is needed) and must also meet the language requirement of the university and programme for its teaching language. They must meet the entry requirements of the chosen university and programme.

Exclusions: anyone who already receives another scholarship or financial support from the Chinese government or other organisations cannot hold this award.

Some universities add their own rules. For example, Shanghai University of Finance and Economics (undergraduate 2026) asks for age 18 to 25, HSK 5 with a score of at least 180, and a CSCA result; applicants with a Chinese parent or who emigrated from mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau or Taiwan must meet the Ministry of Education rules for such cases. Shanghai Jiao Tong University (graduate 2027) says applicants may apply through the university or through a Chinese embassy or consulate abroad, but not both.
age_experience_notes: Age should generally be 25 or under (undergraduate), 35 or under (master's), 40 or under (doctoral), and under 23 for pre-college. The official pages state no work-experience requirement.
funding_summary: Type A covers tuition, accommodation, a living allowance and comprehensive medical insurance. Type B covers tuition and comprehensive medical insurance. Funding runs for the approved length of study; the Commission pages give no fixed number of years. Shanghai University of Finance and Economics states that its undergraduate award lasts the standard 4-year programme length. Every recipient is evaluated each year and keeps the award only if the evaluation is passed. Per-level amounts (2027 intake, as published by Shanghai Maritime University): Type A living allowance of RMB 2,500 a month for undergraduate, RMB 3,000 for master's and RMB 3,500 for doctoral students, paid for 12 months a year; medical insurance RMB 800 a year.
programmes_note: The Commission pages list no fields of study; the scheme works through the programmes that each participating university offers to international students. Funding tiers depend on three discipline classes: class 1 is philosophy, economics, law, education, literature, history and management; class 2 is science, engineering and agriculture; class 3 is medicine and arts. The money for each class is shown only in an image on the official page. Pre-college recipients receive the Type A rate for class 1 undergraduate programmes. To find programmes, use the programme lists of each university on the Study in Shanghai platform.
institutions_note: 31 institutions take part (listed in Appendix 2 of the Commission guide). Applicants choose a university, apply to it through the Study in Shanghai platform and follow that university's own dates and extra requirements. Application periods differ widely between universities; the platform lists a separate period for each one.

summary.detail: Undergraduate programmes at the 31 listed institutions. Entry: high school diploma or above, generally 25 or under, HSK 4 plus the programme's language requirement. Type A and Type B are both available. Type A (2027 intake, Shanghai Maritime University): living allowance RMB 2,500 a month for 12 months a year, free on-campus accommodation in a two-person room, medical insurance RMB 800 a year, tuition exempt.

Each university sets its own list, translation and notarisation rules and application fee (for example RMB 830 at Shanghai University of Finance and Economics undergraduate 2026, RMB 800 at Shanghai Jiao Tong University graduate 2027).

application_steps.title: Choose a Shanghai university and check its programme and dates
application_steps.detail: Pick one of the 31 participating institutions and a programme that fits your level and language. Each university has its own application period and entry rules, listed on the Study in Shanghai platform and on the university's international admissions pages. The Commission says applications are generally accepted from February to April, but several universities open earlier or later (for example Shanghai Maritime University accepts 2027 applications from 1 December 2026 to 30 April 2027).

application_steps.title: Take required tests and prepare your documents
application_steps.detail: Prepare your HSK certificate and the language proof for the programme. Undergraduate applicants at some universities also need a CSCA result (Shanghai University of Finance and Economics asked for it before 31 March 2026). Collect transcripts, degree certificates, passport and any extra items the university lists.

application_steps.title: Submit the university application and flag the scholarship
application_steps.detail: Apply online to the university and indicate that you also apply for the Shanghai Government Scholarship (for example under Financial Support at Shanghai University of Finance and Economics, or by selecting scholarship application through the university at Shanghai Jiao Tong University). Some universities require the signed scholarship application form to be uploaded. Application fees are set by the university and are not refunded in the examples read. You may apply either through the university or through a Chinese embassy or consulate, not both (Shanghai Jiao Tong University).

application_steps.title: University admission review and interview
application_steps.detail: The university reviews your application, and may hold an online interview (Shanghai University of Finance and Economics held undergraduate interviews in mid-April 2026). At that university, scholarship shortlisting happens only for applicants who first receive an admission offer, and eligibility is checked automatically from the application form.

application_steps.title: Scholarship decision and award level
application_steps.detail: Awards are merit-based (academic record, test scores, activities and similar), not based on financial need, at the university read. Selection normally takes place in late May or early June at that university, and applicants with no reply by 30 June 2026 should assume they were unsuccessful. Shanghai Jiao Tong University reviews documents after the deadline, sets the award level and publishes results only in its application system, without separate written notices. Applicants who are not nominated for the Chinese Government Scholarship there are automatically considered for the Shanghai award.

application_steps.title: Visa, enrolment and registration
application_steps.detail: After you receive the scholarship, the university guides you through visa application, enrolment, registration, health certification and the residence permit, following the rules that apply. Universities in principle provide dormitory housing in the first year.

application_steps.title: Pass the yearly evaluation to keep the award
application_steps.detail: Each year the university evaluates your academic performance, attitude to study, attendance and conduct, and reports the result to the Shanghai Municipal Education Commission. If you pass, you keep the award for the next year. If you fail, it may be suspended or ended from the next academic year. Recipients also take part in activities such as Experiencing China and Studying in Shanghai arranged by the Commission and universities.
